Workpaper WP-015
1) Staff obtained the project registry extract for the twelve reforestation initiatives cited in the offering memorandum and inspected the parcel identifiers, legal descriptions, and geofence coordinates; the registry returned no records matching any of the twelve identifiers; the absence of registered land parcels for all cited projects remains an unremediated exception.
2) Staff compared the 48 GPS plot files in the due-diligence data room against national geodetic benchmark databases and cross-checked field metadata against known surveyor credentials; the files failed geodetic reconciliation for all 48 plots and listed surveyor licenses that do not exist in the issuing authority's public roster; the provenance of every GPS dataset is unresolved.
3) Staff inspected the 214 satellite imagery exhibits, their timestamps, cloud-cover annotations, and spectral vegetation indices; the imagery exhibited duplicated cloud patterns across unrelated dates and showed vegetation indices inconsistent with the claimed species composition for the target region; the authenticity and temporal integrity of the satellite evidence remain unexplained.
4) Staff traced each of the 36 verifier reports to the issuing verification body's public credentialing database, reviewed the signatory fields, and confirmed the accreditation scope; the issuing entities do not hold MRV accreditations, three signatories are deceased, and the report numbering sequences contain gaps; the validity of all third-party verification opinions is open.
5) Staff performed a walkthrough of the buyer due-diligence file, testing the representation-and-warranty schedule against the underlying title, insurance, and bank confirmation documents; the R&W schedule contains 14 statements with no supporting document reference, and the insurance certificates reference a broker with no verifiable existence; the completeness of the sales narrative's evidentiary chain is not closed.
6) Staff interviewed the four sales personnel referenced in the communications log and compared their stated roles against employment records and commission payment ledgers; two interviewees were not on the payroll for the relevant period and commission payments trace to accounts outside the company's banking relationship; the authorship and authorization of the buyer-facing representations remain unidentified.
7) Staff recomputed the carbon tonnage claims from the plot area, growth models, and sequestration assumptions in the technical annex; the recomputation variance exceeded 400% for nine of twelve projects and the model coefficients matched no published methodology version; the quantitative basis of the credit volume claims is unsupported.
